st: Cut the tomatoes into chunky pieces and put them in a large bowl.
Add the cucumber slices, sliced pepper and red onion.
Sprinkle with salt and toss lightly. Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the vegetables release their juices.
Whisk the oil and vinegar in a small cup and pour it over the vegetables. Toss gently.
Pile the salad onto plates or a serving bowl and scatter the parsley on top.
Cover the top generously with the grated cheese like a snowy blanket and serve right away.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and brush a 9 by 13 baking dish with melted butter.
Whisk the eggs, yogurt and baking soda in a large bowl. Stir in the feta, leaving a few lumps.
Lay 2 sheets of phyllo in the dish, letting them hang over the sides a bit. Brush lightly with butter.
Spoon a quarter of the filling over the sheets. Add 2 more sheets, crumpling them loosely, and repeat until the filling is gone.
Finish with 2 sheets of phyllo on top, tuck in the edges, and brush with all the remaining butter.
Cut the banitsa into squares with a sharp knife before baking so it slices cleanly later.
Bake for 40 minutes until puffed and deep golden brown, and the center is set.
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve warm or at room temperature.
Peel and dice the cucumbers, put them in a bowl, and sprinkle with a little salt.
Mash the garlic with a pinch of salt into a paste.
In a large bowl, whisk the yogurt with the cold water until smooth and pourable.
Stir in the cucumbers, garlic and most of the dill.
Add [[1 tbsp]] of the oil and taste for salt.
Chill for at least 15 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with the walnuts, remaining dill and a drizzle of the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Put the pork, beef, onion, garlic, cumin, paprika, pepper, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Add the cold water and knead the mixture with your hands for 5 minutes until sticky and well combined.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight, so the flavors develop.
Wet your hands and shape the meat into 8 finger-shaped sausages, pressing them to hold together.
Heat a grill, grill pan or broiler to high and brush the grate or pan lightly with oil.
Cook the kebapche for 4 minutes per side, turning gently, until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with bread, chopped onion and fries.

ing: crusts removed, soaked in water and squeezed
st: Tear the soaked bread into small pieces in a large bowl.
Add the pork, beef, onion, egg, cumin, parsley, pepper and salt.
Mix with your hands for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture is well combined and slightly sticky.
Cover and chill for 20 minutes to firm up.
Wet your hands and shape into 8 flat patties about the size of your palm.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat, or heat a grill to medium.
Cook the patties for 5 to 6 minutes per side until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot with fries, salad or bread.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Put the peppers and eggplant on a lined baking sheet.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blistered and the flesh is soft.
Put the peppers in a covered bowl to steam for 15 minutes. Then peel the peppers and eggplant and remove the seeds and stems.
Meanwhile, cut the tomatoes into chunks and simmer them in a pot over medium heat for 10 minutes. Press through a sieve to remove skins and seeds.
Finely chop or pulse the roasted peppers and eggplant in a food processor to a coarse puree.
Heat the oil in a wide heavy pot. Add the vegetable puree, the tomato puree, sugar and salt.
Cook over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often, until very thick and the oil begins to separate.
Stir in the garlic and vinegar and cook for 3 minutes more.
Cool and store in clean jars in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Serve as a spread on bread.

ing: peeled and cut into small cubes
st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a 9 by 13 baking dish.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the pork and brown for 8 minutes, breaking it up.
Stir in the tomatoes, paprika, savory, pepper and salt and cook for 8 minutes until the liquid is mostly gone.
Mix in the potatoes and spread everything evenly in the baking dish.
Whisk the eggs, yogurt and flour until completely smooth, and pour the mixture over the top.
Bake for 40 minutes until the topping is set and golden. The meat should be at 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
Cut out the core of the cabbage. Simmer the whole head in salted water for 10 minutes, then peel off the soft outer leaves as they loosen.
Trim the thick rib from each leaf and cut large leaves in half.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Stir in [[1 tsp]] paprika and cook for 30 seconds.
Mix the onion with the pork, rice, savory, pepper and salt in a bowl.
Put a spoonful of filling at the base of each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Line a heavy pot with spare cabbage leaves and pack the rolls in snug layers.
Mix the tomatoes with [[1 tsp]] paprika, [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[2 cups]] hot water, and pour over the rolls.
Set a plate on top to keep them down, cover, and simmer on low for 70 minutes until the rice and meat are done (160°F / 71°C inside).
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve with yogurt.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C).
Heat the oil in a heavy oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork in batches for 6 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the mushrooms and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes, wine, water, bay leaf, savory, pepper and salt.
Return the pork to the pot, bring to a simmer, then cover.
Bake for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring once, until the pork is very tender and the sauce is thick.
Remove the bay leaf, taste for salt, and serve with bread or potatoes.
Put the tripe in a pot, cover with water, and boil for 15 minutes. Drain, rinse well and discard that water.
Return the tripe to the pot with [[8 cups]] fresh water, the bay leaves, peppercorns and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 2 hours 30 minutes until very tender, skimming off any foam.
Lift out the tripe and slice it into thin strips. Return it to the pot.
Melt the butter in a small pan, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then take off the heat and stir in the paprika.
Stir the paprika butter into the soup, then add the milk. Simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Mix the crushed garlic with the vinegar in a small bowl.
Ladle the soup into bowls and let everyone add garlic vinegar and extra paprika to taste.
Mix the warm water, yeast and sugar and leave for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt. Add the yeast mixture, yogurt, egg and [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Mix and knead for 5 minutes into a very soft, slightly sticky dough.
Cover and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Oil your hands and the counter. Pull off egg-sized pieces of dough and gently stretch each to a flat round.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a wide pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the mekitsi 2 or 3 at a time for 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels, dust generously with powdered sugar, and serve warm with jam or crumbled white cheese.

ing: 3 for the dough and 1 for the wash
st: Stir the yeast, [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar and the warm milk together and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, remaining sugar, salt and lemon zest. Add the yeast mixture, 3 eggs and the vanilla.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Knead in the soft butter a little at a time until the dough is silky and not sticky.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour 30 minutes until doubled.
Knead in the raisins gently, divide the dough into 3 equal pieces and roll each into a long rope.
Braid the ropes together and place the braid on a parchment-lined tray, tucking the ends under.
Cover and rise for 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Beat the last egg and brush it over the bread.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden, covering with foil if it browns too fast. Cool on a rack.
Roast the eggplants, peppers and tomato at 450°F for 40 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blackened and the flesh is soft.
Cover the vegetables in a bowl for 10 minutes so the skins loosen, then peel them.
Drain the eggplant flesh in a sieve for 10 minutes to remove bitter liquid, then chop finely.
Chop the peppers and tomato finely and combine with the eggplant in a bowl.
Stir in the garlic, parsley, oil, [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and salt until a chunky spread forms.
Chill for 1 hour and serve on toasted bread or alongside grilled meat.
nt: Roasted in the oven, then chopped and dressed
Best swap: char the vegetables on a grill or gas flame instead of the oven for a deeper smoke.
